newsitem.title: USA: Iridium World gains after IPO.
newsitem.headline: Iridium World gains after IPO.

text.p: Iridium World Communications Ltd shares rose on in heavy trading after the initial public offering of the company, which plans to develop a global satellite network linking wireless telephones.
Shares rose 2-3/8 to 22-3/8 on their first day of trading from their IPO price of $20, the midpoint of price talk of $19 to $21 a share.

The deal was oversubscribed, allowing Iridium to offer even more shares -- 12 million -- from its original plan to sell ten million. That meant the company raise an additional $40 million. The IPO raised roughly $240 million total.
Iridium has said it plans to use some of the proceeds to develop its global service via a $3.4 billion system of 66 low-orbit satellites.
It plans to launch seven satellites in mid-June and despite some prior delays, Iridium said it plans to roll out its commercial service in September 1998.
Iridium World represents about an eight percent stake in Iridium LLC, a consortium including Motorola Inc, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp and Raytheon Co.
The stock was one of the most heavily traded issues on the Nasdaq on its first day of trading.

"We believe that Iridium's global satellite network will have tremendous future potential as it spans the globe and provides interoperability with all cellular networks," said Monda Eraiba, a semiconductor and electronics analyst for Gruntal & Co.

She said the IPO will also benefit Motorola, which has been drained financially by its heavy investment in Iridium. The offering cuts Motorola's stake to 25 percent. Motorola shares slipped 1/2 to 66-5/8.
